statement: Find the equation of the tangent to the circle $x^2+y^2=25$ at the point $(3,4)$.
solution:
Differentiating implicitly, $2x+2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{x}{y}$. At $(3,4)$ the gradient is $-\dfrac34$.

The tangent is therefore
$$y-4=-\frac34(x-3)\quad\Rightarrow\quad 4y-16=-3x+9\quad\Rightarrow\quad 3x+4y=25.$$
(Indeed $3\cdot3+4\cdot4=25$, confirming the point lies on the circle.)
hints: Write the line through (3,4) with that gradient.
